messages:
maria_cho: Heads up, after the AZ NAT failover earlier we started seeing intermittent failures to the private interface endpoint that fronts our ELB proxy for S3/ECR. Some pods get 504s during large pulls. :eyes:
infra-bot: ALERT 2030502469 privatelink-ep-az1 unhealthy -> route-check suggested
oncall-sre: can you paste an example curl/nslookup? wondering if this is DNS or SNAT
maria_cho: quick debug: tried from a tracer pod in the affected AZ:
```
$ dig @10.0.0.2 vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com +short
10.111.22.33
```
then curl to the VIP (ELB IP returned) times out intermittently. tcpdump shows SYN->SYN-ACK sometimes, other times server never responds after NAT translation.
kevin_lin: suspecting asymmetric path after NAT failover + transit-gw propagation delay. If ENI for the interface endpoint stayed in the old AZ routing might be hitting a transit path without reverse path to the ENI.
samir_patel: also check security group egress rules — interface endpoints are stateful but if the ELB proxy rewrites source to an ephemeral port range outside allowed egress we can drop return. Did NAT mappings change?
julia_pm: this is causing customer-facing latency for model artifact pulls, priority high. What quick mitigation?
oncall-sre: quick mitigation -> pin routes in the subnet RT to force local NAT gateway in that AZ and temporarily bypass TGW. Runbook suggestion below.
kevin_lin: commands I ran:
```
# list ENIs for the vpce
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters \ 
  Name=description,Values="*vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f*" --query 'NetworkInterfaces[*].{Id:NetworkInterfaceId,Subnet:SubnetId,AZ:AvailabilityZone}'

# check route table associations for subnet
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0abc123
```
Found endpoint ENI in az1 but subnet routes in az1 were propagating to transit-gw attachment in az2 after the NGW failover.
maria_cho: confirmed: route table had a propagated route 0.0.0.0/0 -> tgw-attach-0ffff which points to another AZ's NAT. ENI remains local so return path mismatches.
samir_patel: workaround applied: removed propagation for that RT and added explicit 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-az1 temporarily. After that pulls stabilized.
julia_pm: please capture exact steps and time, we need an incident note for postmortem and customer comms.
oncall-sre: recorded it in incident tracker and added a short checklist: 1) identify endpoint ENI AZ 2) confirm subnet RT targets 3) if propagated TGW present, add explicit nat route 4) monitor for 5m
kevin_lin: longer term fix options: a) update endpoint to create ENIs in all AZs we actually use (some automation currently prunes low-usage ENIs), b) enforce route propagation guardrails on TGW attachments that overlap privatelink subnets, c) make ELB proxy respect X-Forwarded-For and avoid source rewrite when calling VPC endpoints.
maria_cho: note: there was also a split-horizon DNS forwarder (forwarder in az1 had stale cached VPCE private IP) — we shortened TTL to 30s as a safety. Dig after TTL change shows correct ENI IPs.
```
$ dig @10.0.0.2 vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com +short
10.111.22.33
10.111.22.34
```
kevin_lin: added a temporary health-check rule on the ELB to prefer AZ-local ENIs by increasing path weight for AZ-local targets. Not ideal but reduces cross-AZ bounce.
samir_patel: we should also audit SG egress ephemeral ranges — adding 32768-65535 to allowed egress for the ELB->vpce security group fixed a few stuck connections in our tests.
julia_pm: assign a follow-up: eng-infra to implement TGW propagation guardrails + devex to update deploy automation for endpoint ENI retention policy.
kevin_lin: created ticket INF-4122 with plan and rollback.
oncall-sre: monitoring logs for 15m, so far no 504 spikes. Will close thread if stable. :thumbsup:
maria_cho: thanks everyone — capture the runbook steps in confluence and tag me for verification.
kevin_lin: FYI for postmortem: cost note — the transient NAT path increased cross-AZ data egress and we saw ~12% spike in NAT cost for the hour. Include cost impact in the incident report.
infra-bot: Incident INF-4122 status -> monitoring (2030502745)
maria_cho: closing here once conf doc is updated, leaving link in the ticket.
